summary: Records and outputs a sliding or growing history window of input channel values, with the last sample representing the current frame.
key_concepts: Trail CHOP outputs the history of input channel values over a sliding or growing window.
The history window runs backward from the current frame, and the last sample is the current input value.
Grow Length records an arbitrary increasing history instead of a fixed-size window.
Capture can record a continuous time slice every cook or only when the input cooks, which is useful for sparse events.
Resample and Set Rate can reshape the output sample count and output sample rate.
Changing input channel count or names clears the stored trail history and starts recording again.

key_params.name: growlength
key_params.note: Let recording length grow with timeline

key_params.name: wlengthunit
key_params.note: Window units: samples, frames, or seconds

key_params.name: capture
key_params.note: Capture time slice every cook or only when input cooks

common_gotchas: If input channel count or names change, Trail CHOP clears its stored trails and starts over.
Use Replace CHOP upstream to create stand-in values when names may disappear temporarily.
Time Slice capture records a continuous sliding log; Only When Input Cooks is better for sparse events.
Grow Length can create very long histories in long-running systems.
Use Record CHOP when explicit gated recording and storage control is needed.
